purpose: Assess whether the observed 1/2/5 km change in the cross-species A x H interaction is more extreme than expected from finite-sample fluctuation under the same block-preserving trait-association null.

permutation.strata: species x frozen V3 spatial block
permutation.unit: one complete multi-radius trait tuple per site: [A1,H1,AH1,A2,H2,AH2,A5,H5,AH5]
permutation.scheme: Within each species x spatial block, apply one site permutation to the entire 1/2/5 km trait tuple, preserving cross-radius trait correlation. Outcomes, site identities, observation data and forcing remain fixed. Refit the complete V3 model independently at each radius.

diagnostics: P_null(sign switch 2km negative to 5km positive AND contrast >= observed)
P_null(median_2km < median_1km < median_5km AND range >= observed)

interpretation_rule.strong_scale_dependence: Use ecological scale-dependence language only if the joint directional sign-switch-plus-contrast null probability <=0.05.
interpretation_rule.weak_or_null: If >0.05, describe the radius sensitivity as instability compatible with sampling/permutation fluctuation, not as an ecological discovery.
interpretation_rule.regardless: Always report the raw 1/2/5 km point estimates and keep 2 km as the frozen primary scale.

boundary: This is a post-inference interpretation diagnostic, not a new primary test.
No radius is promoted or dropped based on this result.
The same permutation map is used jointly across radii to preserve multi-scale trait covariance.
